correctness.rationale: On each smooth sign quadrant, direct differentiation gives a Jacobian with characteristic polynomial \(\lambda(\lambda^2-T)\). Eliminating \(x\) from the equilibrium conic and \(T=0\) gives the two displayed sextics. Exact rational Sturm sequences prove each sextic has exactly two real roots and isolate them in the stated intervals; sign checks discard the root lying on the wrong sign branch in each case. Continuity and exact representative signs then classify all four smooth arcs. The bundled verifier replays the elimination and root counts without floating-point assumptions. The nondifferentiable axis points are explicitly excluded.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete local transverse-type map of the smooth part of a published nonisolated equilibrium curve at the parameter values used to exhibit chaos. It shows that the same curve contains both normally hyperbolic saddle segments and spectrally elliptic segments, and locates the two transition points exactly by algebraic equations rather than trajectory sampling. This is structurally useful for understanding which parts of the equilibrium continuum can seed local instability, for organizing continuation or basin studies, and for distinguishing equilibrium-manifold geometry from numerical attractor behavior. It is more informative than recomputing one eigenvalue table or one parameter scan.
